_note:
The status kubectl prints for a pod, in the region where both evaluators claim the same answer. Rust derives it for every live pod (src-tauri/src/resources/types/pod_display.rs); TypeScript derives it for a manifest somebody pasted into the infrastructure builder, where no cluster read happened (src/features/infrastructure/utils.ts). Two implementations in two languages, and this file is what holds them to one answer.

FOUR THINGS ARE OUTSIDE IT, and a case that touches one belongs in the Rust tests alone. Three because TypeScript does not implement them: an init container blocking, a pod-level reason, a deletionTimestamp. The fourth because the two disagree ON PURPOSE: an app container waiting `PodInitializing`. Rust keeps it — its app-container loop does not filter it, matching kubectl — while TypeScript falls through to the phase, because this canvas cannot read init containers and `Pending` is nearer the truth than `PodInitializing` where kubectl would print `Init:0/2`. That is argued in `utils.test.ts`'s "falls back to the phase when no container says otherwise". Adding it here would pin a disagreement, not an agreement.

cases.name: a container waiting for a reason names the pod
the first container's verdict is the one that stands
a running container leaves the phase standing
a terminated container names its reason
a terminated container with no reason names its exit code
a container killed by a signal names the signal
